A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAEMark study. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite the revised title and organization. v2 also includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection, text-quality, latency, scaling, robustness, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same candidate selection, CDF normalization, SAE Feature Concentration Score, background masking, alignment filters, and t-test detection. Diagram and pseudocode wording edits do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate C4, LCSTS, MBPP, PandaLM, and BIGGen-Bench, retaining English, Chinese, code generation, and instruction-following coverage. The evaluated attack scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains KGW, EXP, UPV, Unigram, DIP, Unbiased, SynthID, SWEET, and Waterfall. Table 3 and the latency and multi-bit comparisons retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Sample counts, detection at 1% FPR, quality judges, backbone models, and Appendix B settings remain unchanged, including N=50, M=10, K=15, and temperature 0.7. Figure 4's revised end-to-end latency label does not document a changed measurement procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain candidate-count sensitivity, alignment-filter and feature-distribution ablations, and background masking analysis. Appendix E retains the same structure-preserving versus structure-disrupting attacks and context-aware substitutions through 50% intensity.

E5.justification: The detector's t-test and Figure 3's normality tests and p-values are unchanged. The new checklist reiterates existing statistical testing; it adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or performance uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 match numerically, including SAEMark F1 scores of 99.7%, 99.2%, and 66.3% on C4, LCSTS, and MBPP, respectively. The latency, scaling, robustness, and ablation figures retain the same reported values and curves.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the Gaussian assumption, the single-unit embedding-success bound, and the FCS definition remain unchanged. Moving the theoretical analysis from Section 3.2 to Section 3.3 introduces no new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction drops v1's claim that theoretical guarantees scale with text length. The abstract and conclusion recast embedding-success probability versus compute as watermark accuracy versus compute, while retaining the central multilingual, multi-bit, API-compatible watermarking contribution.

C2.justification: The stated collusion-resistance goal narrows from preventing removal or forgery to preventing forgery. The privacy scope changes from avoiding storage of sensitive content to avoiding storage of LLM-generated text. Result interpretations and Appendix A's substantive limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checklist item 13 newly reports repository documentation and one-line reproduction scripts. This is an additional disclosure, not evidence of a newly available release. Appendix B's implementation settings and the code/data destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds PURE and removes Is Best-of-N the Best of Them? and RewardAnything. The renamed code-generation reference retains arXiv identifier 2412.15118 and is the same work. Positioning relative to existing watermarking methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, SAE background is condensed into Related Work, Task Definition moves into Methodology, and robustness and ablations become one subsection. Together with edited introductory and concluding prose and the appended NeurIPS checklist, this substantially reorganizes the document.

P2.justification: The conference format revises front matter, headings, and layout throughout. Figure 1 moves to the first page, Figure 3 expands from a small wrapped figure to full width, and tables and appendix figures are rearranged. Captions, labels, and table emphasis also change; the underlying displays retain their data.

improvement.justification: v2 improves Figure 3's legibility and reorganizes the exposition, while retaining the same methods, derivations, experiments, results, and substantive limitations. The checklist adds little reproducibility detail and does not supply the concrete compute information its answers suggest. These modest presentation benefits and reporting weaknesses leave overall quality essentially unchanged.
